title: Design Scalable React State Architecture
description: Choose between Redux, React Query, context, and server state for a large React app.

data.text: You are designing a SaaS dashboard with 40+ feature modules. Multiple teams ship features independently. The app must support optimistic updates, offline queueing, and real-time collaboration.
Use a single Redux store for everything. Simple initially, but coupling grows with team size.

data.title: Monolithic Redux Store

data.text: Approach 2: Modular State with React Query + Context
Keep server state in React Query, local UI state in feature-scoped context, and cross-cutting concerns in a small global store.

data.title: Modular State Architecture

data.text: Each micro-frontend owns its state shell. The host only coordinates routing and shared auth.

data.title: Micro-Frontend State Isolation
data.code:
// shell/App.tsx
<BrowserRouter>
  <AuthProvider>
    <MicroFrontend
      name="orders"
      host="https://orders.example.com"
      scope="orders"
    />
    <MicroFrontend
      name="inventory"
      host="https://inventory.example.com"
      scope="inventory"
    />
  </AuthProvider>
</BrowserRouter>

data.title: Recommended
data.text: For most large apps: React Query for server state, Zustand or Context for UI state, and avoid a single monolithic store.
